claims: Above it you pay 15c for each dollar up to $45,000
It's a zero-rate band that every resident gets once per income year
whys: The rate and the bracket ceiling are typed into the prose, not taken from the tax scale constants. 15% is right for 2026-27, but the legislated rate falls to 14% from 1 July 2027, so this goes stale silently when SITE_CONFIG.financialYear moves on.

Scope is too wide: the same page (line 181) says part-year residents get a reduced, pro-rated threshold, not the full {T} band. Could read 'every full-year resident'. Left unchanged because it narrows a factual claim.

claims: At the {FY} rate of 15% above {T}, ... cancels the tax on the next {formatAUD(LITO.maxOffset / 0.15)} of income
whys: Both the printed 15% and the 0.15 divisor are hard-coded, while FY and the NIL figure are derived. When the second bracket rate changes (14% from 1 July 2027) the sentence and the computed slice will disagree with the {NIL} figure.

claims: answer Yes only if total income from all sources will be less than the threshold
whys: Boundary is inconsistent across the page: line 156 says 'less than the threshold', while line 175 and the FAQ answers (tax-free-threshold-faqs.ts lines 29 and 33) say '{T} or less'. One wording should be checked against the ATO TFN declaration and multiple-jobs pages and used everywhere.
constants: none (prose); ATO QC50527 / TFN declaration question 9

claims: For work-related expenses under $300 in total, you are not required to provide written evidence
whys: The ATO wording is a total claim of $300 or less, so 'under $300' leaves out a claim of exactly $300. The $300 and $150 laundry figures are also typed into the prose rather than coming from a constant.

claims: Even if you earned less than the tax-free threshold, lodging gets you a full refund of the PAYG tax withheld
whys: A full refund holds only for a full-year resident (the threshold is pro-rated for part-year residents, and minors' unearned income is taxed differently). The tax-return-2026 FAQ (line 52) already gives these exceptions, but this page does not.
